cover.headline: Three US exclusivities made FY26; competition is now taking them away. The base business is better than ever, but the price already pays for the replacements
cover.lead: Lupin is India's eighth-largest drug maker and the third-largest generic company in the US by prescriptions. FY26 was a record (EPS ₹116.7, EBITDA margin 29%) because three US products had little or no competition: generic Spiriva (an inhaler), Mirabegron and Tolvaptan. Brokers estimate the three were about half of earnings. Q1FY27 was another record (US $366mn, margin 30%), but management guides US sales back to $250-280mn a quarter as Apotex and Teva enter Tolvaptan, and an EBITDA margin of ~25% for FY27. The stock is ₹2,030 (19% below its July high): 21.2x our FY27E EPS and 20.3x FY28E, with ₹2,831 cr of net cash. The street values Lupin on **P/E (22-26x forward EPS)**. We forecast EPS of ₹95.9 / 99.9 / 105.0 for FY27-29E, a little below consensus (₹101 / 103 for FY27-28E). Applying **19x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹102.6** (Lupin's own forward median of 17.6x since 2021 on EPS before exceptional items, leaving out the FY23 trough, re-rated by the pharma sector's +8.2%) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,492, DCF ₹1,715. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The windfall is being competed away, on schedule
arguments.p: Tolvaptan (sole generic since May-2025) gets two rivals from Q2FY27 and possibly a third in September; Mirabegron got a third generic in Q1 and broad entry from Sep-2027; Spiriva has no generic rival yet but its market is moving to the Respimat version. Management guides US sales of $1.1-1.2bn for FY27 (FY26 US$1,318mn). We model US$1,170mn / 1,200mn / 1,150mn for FY27-29E and EPS −18% in FY27E.

arguments.h: The business underneath is much stronger than in FY23
arguments.p: Outside the US, organic growth was over 20% in Q1FY27: India +13.9% (prescriptions +15.1% vs the market's 13.5%, 67% chronic), Europe +83% with VISUfarma, Brazil +117% in local currency. Gross margin is 74.6% against ~59% in FY23. That is why we expect margins to settle at ~23-24%, not to fall back to the 10% of FY23.

arguments.h: The replacements are real but arrive late
arguments.p: The apixaban oral suspension was tentatively approved on 25-Sep-2026 and should launch around summer 2027 with 10-12 months before generics; pegfilgrastim (a biosimilar) launches in H2FY27; Lupin won its ivacaftor patent case in August; Dulera, Spiriva Respimat and more biosimilars follow in FY28-29. Management expects US growth to resume in FY28. Emkay calls that optimistic; Citi sees US sales falling to $975mn by FY29.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price already assumes the replacements work
arguments.p: At 20.3x FY28E Lupin trades above its own 17.6x forward median since 2021 (trough year left out): the market paid ~16x forward when the forward year held the windfall. 19x Sep-28E gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, −4% from here and within 1% of the SELL line. EV/EBITDA is kinder (₹2,492), the DCF harsher (₹1,715); the street's ₹2,500 median target is 24.3x consensus FY28E EPS.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter with Apotex and Teva in Tolvaptan; US sales against the $250-280mn guide and margin against ~25% for the year.
US launches in H2FY27: pegfilgrastim (via Valorum), ranibizumab, raltegravir (exclusive first-to-file), dalbavancin and fluticasone nasal spray.
Apixaban oral suspension: final approval and launch (commercial quantities from Jan-2027, launch around summer 2027); ivacaftor launch after the Aug-2026 court win.
Competition: a possible fourth Tolvaptan generic; broad Mirabegron entry from Sep-2027; any generic Spiriva approval.
USFDA: Pithampur Unit-2 (OAI) remediation; warning letters at Tarapur and Mandideep; use of cash for specialty acquisitions.

sections.title: What Lupin does: a US generics company with an Indian branded franchise, now growing in Europe and emerging markets

blocks.p: Lupin makes and sells medicines in 100+ countries from 15 plants. **United States** (₹11,678 cr in FY26, 42% of sales; $1318mn) sells 149 generic products: inhalers (generic Spiriva, albuterol, Xopenex), tablets and capsules, and a growing list of injectables; it is No.3 in US generics by prescriptions and No.1 in 56 products. **India** (₹8,114 cr, 30%) sells branded prescription drugs through ~11,300 sales staff, mostly for chronic diseases (diabetes, heart, respiratory: 67% of the portfolio), plus consumer health (LupinLife), diagnostics labs and digital health. **Other developed markets** (₹3,244 cr, 12%: Europe, Canada, Australia) and **emerging markets** (₹3,483 cr, 13%: Brazil, South Africa, Philippines, Mexico) sell branded generics and specialty products. **API** (₹969 cr, 4%) sells drug ingredients, where Lupin is a global leader in anti-TB drugs and cephalosporin antibiotics.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Lupin is two businesses with different economics. The US is a pipeline business: it earns large profits from a few hard-to-copy products for a year or two, then has to replace them. Everything else (India, Europe, emerging markets, API: 58% of sales) is a steadier branded franchise growing ~12-15%. FY23-26 showed how violently the first can swing the total: margin from 10% to 29%.

sections.title: Industry: US generics pay only for complexity and exclusivity; India grows steadily

blocks.p: **United States.** US generics: low-single-digit price erosion on the base portfolio (Lupin: 'mid single digit price decline due to additional competition in select products' in Q1FY27). Profits come from products few can copy - inhalers, long-acting injectables, peptides, biosimilars, first-to-file patent challenges - and last only until rivals arrive. Lupin is No.3 in US generics by prescriptions (~5.0% of generic TRx), No.1 in 56 products and top-3 in 112 (IQVIA, quarter to Jun-26). Approval also depends on plant inspections: a warning letter or an 'Official Action Indicated' rating stops new approvals from that plant, which is why Lupin's compliance record matters as much as its R&D.

**India.** Indian pharma market (IPM): +13.5% in Q1FY27 (IQVIA, as quoted by Lupin and Cipla) and +11.1% on MAT Jun-26 (IQVIA via Kotak Neo); Pharmarack: Aug-2026 +10.7%, CY2026 forecast raised to 11.3%. Chronic therapies grow faster than acute (Lupin chronic +21.5% vs IPM chronic +16.8% in Q1FY27). Lupin is No.8 in the IPM (IQVIA MAT Jun-26): No.1 in anti-TB, No.2 in respiratory, No.3 in cardiac and anti-diabetes (ICRA, company). Price increases on drugs under India's price-control list are capped at the wholesale-price index each April.

**Europe, emerging markets and API.** Europe: budget pressure (Germany doubling some rebates) but biosimilar substitution incentives rising (France); ophthalmology biosimilars in Germany outside AOK tenders. Lupin's European sales passed USD200mn in FY26 and grew 83% in Q1FY27 with VISUfarma. Emerging markets: Brazil (+117% in local currency in Q1FY27 on dapagliflozin and empagliflozin), South Africa (Pharma Dynamics, No.7 generic company), Philippines (Multicare, 56.28%), Mexico (Grin). Semaglutide launches in South Africa (FY27) and Brazil (filing FY27). API: ₹969 cr (4% of sales) in FY26, down 18% as more output went captive; global leader in cephalosporins and anti-TB APIs; Dabhasa and Vizag API sites moved into Lupin Manufacturing Solutions (ICRA).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Lupin captures the Indian chronic tailwind well and has proven it can win in hard US products. But the US gains are product-by-product and temporary, which is exactly what FY27 shows: the same tailwind that lifted EBITDA margin to 31% in Q2FY26 now runs in reverse as rivals launch.

sections.title: United States: three exclusivities doubled the business; two are now being competed away

blocks.p: Lupin's US business has two layers. The **base**: 149 marketed generics (No.1 in 56, top-3 in 112), led by respiratory (over 20% of the base: albuterol, tiotropium, Xopenex), plus tablets, capsules and a growing injectables list (glucagon, liraglutide, gRisperdal Consta). It suffers low-to-mid single-digit price erosion each year and grows on volume and launches (15 in FY26). The **windfall**: generic Spiriva HandiHaler (first generic, Aug-2023; ~35-38% of the molecule and still no generic rival), Mirabegron (launched at risk in Apr-2024; settled with Astellas in Feb-2026 for $90mn plus a per-unit fee) and Tolvaptan (exclusive first-to-file from May-2025; the only generic for more than a year because rivals had patent and manufacturing hurdles). Lupin does not disclose product sales; brokers put the three at about half of group EPS (PL, Nuvama).

blocks.p: What happens next is mostly known. **Tolvaptan**: Apotex and Teva launch from Q2FY27 and a fourth entrant may follow in September; management expects a "longer tail" because the drug is sold through specialty pharmacies under a safety (REMS) programme and generic penetration is still ~40%, but prices will fall. **Mirabegron**: a third generic arrived in Q1FY27; most settlements allow entry from Sep-2027; Lupin pays Astellas a per-unit fee and amortises the $75mn option until then. **Spiriva**: stable, but the brand market is moving to the Respimat version, which Lupin will only file in FY27.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we model US$1,170mn for FY27E (Q2-Q4: $285 / 260 / 259mn, the upper half of guidance, as Lupin beat its FY26 guidance), US$1,200mn for FY28E (the apixaban oral suspension, pegfilgrastim and exclusivities offset Tolvaptan and Mirabegron) and US$1,150mn for FY29E (apixaban generics arrive). That is above Citi ($975mn base by FY29) and below BOB ($1.33bn). Every $50mn of US sales is ~₹485 cr of revenue and, at ~60% incremental margin for exclusive products, ~₹291 cr of EBITDA (~4.7% of FY28E EPS).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the pipeline is broader than most Indian peers' and the compliance picture improved in FY26-27 (Somerset, Goa, Nagpur, Ankleshwar cleared). But the big items are back-ended and several are one-year opportunities (apixaban before generics, nasal-spray exclusivities). sections.title: India: a chronic-heavy franchise growing ahead of the market (+13.9% in Q1FY27)

blocks.p: Lupin is No.8 in the Indian market (IQVIA MAT Jun-26). About 67% of its prescription portfolio is chronic (diabetes, heart, respiratory, CNS), sold by ~11,300 people (8,700 medical representatives). It leads in anti-TB and is No.2 in respiratory and No.3 in cardiac and diabetes (ICRA) (it markets Lilly's Huminsulin and launched generic semaglutide in Q4FY26). FY26 India sales grew only 7.1% because tender sales to government (the Global Institutional Business) fell and some in-licensed diabetes products lost exclusivity; prescriptions grew 10.6% (IPM 9.9%). Q1FY27 was the best quarter in two years: +13.9%, prescriptions +15.1% vs the market's 13.5%, volume +6.1%.

bullets: **Mix shift:** in-licensed products fell from ~12% of the Rx portfolio (FY25) to ~6%, lifting margins; target 70% chronic by FY31 and one-third of India sales from proprietary products in ten years (in-house, in-licensed and new chemical entities such as Bofanglutide).

**Obesity:** semaglutide injection launched under two brands with a dedicated ~200-person division; oral and vial forms due in H2FY27. Management called the opportunity ~₹1,500 cr for the market in year one and ₹50-60 cr for Lupin, before launch.

**Adjacencies:** diagnostics (7 lakh patients a quarter), digital health and consumer health still lose money; together with CDMO they cost 100-150bp of group margin (CFO); diagnostics to break even in FY28.
**Price control:** many respiratory and anti-infective drugs are under the price-control list; increases are capped each April.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** India is the steadiest part of Lupin. We model +13% / +12% / +12% (FY27-29E), consistent with 1.2-1.3x a market growing ~10-11%, taking India to 33.2% of product sales by FY29E (30% in FY26).

sections.title: Europe, emerging markets and API: a quarter of sales, growing 15-50%

blocks.p: **Other developed markets** (₹3,244 cr in FY26) are Europe, Canada and Australia. Europe passed $200mn in FY26 and grew 83% in Q1FY27 as VISUfarma joined: a Dutch-Italian eye-care company with 60+ products in Italy, Spain, the UK, Germany and France, bought from GHO Capital at an enterprise value of €190mn (~₹1,970 cr, cash) and consolidated from April 2026 (€53mn revenue in 2025; management cites ~25% margins and $100mn+ revenue in two to three years). Lupin also sells inhalers (Luforbec), NaMuscla (a rare-disease drug) and biosimilars through partners such as Sandoz. Management guides Europe +10-20% a year.

**Emerging markets** (₹3,483 cr, +35% in FY26) turned around: Brazil grew 117% in local currency in Q1FY27 on dapagliflozin and empagliflozin; South Africa (Pharma Dynamics) and the Philippines (Multicare, 56.3% owned) are steady; Mexico (Grin) profitable. **API** (₹969 cr) is mostly captive and fluctuates; the Dabhasa and Vizag sites were moved into Lupin Manufacturing Solutions to sell more to third parties.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Lupin has genuine capabilities: it made the first generic Spiriva, won and settled patent fights that rivals lost, and has a chronic-heavy Indian franchise. But in the US those capabilities produce temporary profits, not a moat: every exclusive product attracts rivals within one to three years, and Lupin's compliance record (warning letters in 2017 and still two open today) has cost it launches before. The right way to think about Lupin is a solid Indian and emerging-market business plus a US product machine whose output is lumpy.

sections.title: From two loss years to a record: profit went from a ₹1,528 cr loss (FY22) to ₹5,333 cr (FY26)

blocks.p: Lupin's revenue grew from ₹14,665 cr in FY19 to ₹27,958 cr in FY26 (10% a year), but profit has been a roller-coaster. It made losses in FY20 (impairments, the Japan exit) and FY22 (a ₹1,878 cr US antitrust settlement over the diabetes drug Glumetza and a ₹708 cr write-down of Solosec), and earned only ₹430 cr in FY23 when US prices fell and costs rose. Then three US products that few rivals could copy changed everything: the first generic of the COPD inhaler Spiriva (Aug-2023), the overactive-bladder drug Mirabegron (Apr-2024, launched before the patent fight was settled) and the kidney drug Tolvaptan (May-2025, six months of legal exclusivity that turned into more than a year alone). Profit rose to ₹1,914 cr in FY24, ₹3,282 cr in FY25 and ₹5,333 cr in FY26.

sections.title: Margins: 10% in FY23, 29% in FY26, guided ~25% for FY27 and falling through the year

blocks.p: Lupin's EBITDA margin (operating profit before forex and other income) rose 19 percentage points in three years. Most of it is gross margin: material cost fell from 40.7% of revenue in FY23 to 26.2% in FY26 (Screener), because the new US products sell at prices far above their cost and because India shifted away from low-margin in-licensed products (12% of the Rx portfolio in FY25, 6% now). Staff and other costs also fell as a share of a much larger revenue base. Q1FY27 was another record (gross margin 74.6%, EBITDA margin 30.0%), but management guides ~25% for the full year, which implies ~22-24% for the rest of FY27 as two new generics of Tolvaptan arrive and Mirabegron prices fall.

sections.title: Returns: ROE from −12% (FY22) to 27% (FY26); the windfall cash paid for VISUfarma

blocks.p: Lupin generated ₹13,982 cr of operating cash in FY24-26 and spent ₹4,666 cr on capex (including intangibles and the ₹711 cr Mirabegron licence) and ₹1,096 cr on dividends. The rest turned net debt of ₹2,527 cr (Mar-23) into net cash of ₹4,636 cr (Mar-26). In April 2026 ₹1,970 cr of it went on VISUfarma, a European eye-care company (enterprise value €190mn, €53mn revenue in 2025), so net cash was ₹2,831 cr in June. Return on equity was 26.9% in FY26 and the company's own ROCE 28.4%; we expect ROE to fall to ~15-18% as profit drops and cash builds.

sections.title: Earnings quality: one-off charges keep recurring, forex flatters the headline, licences sit below EBITDA

bullets: **"One-offs" that keep coming.** FY22: ₹1,878 cr Glumetza antitrust settlement and a ₹708 cr Solosec impairment. FY26: a net exceptional charge of ₹558 cr: antitrust provision (us generic-drug litigation) −₹582 cr; mirabegron settlement, one-time payment (usd15mn) −₹137 cr; new labour codes (gratuity, leave) −₹51 cr; transpire bio settlement income (usd10mn) +₹89 cr; arbitration award income and provision reversal (lupin atlantis) +₹123 cr. The antitrust provision is not finished: one case settled for $30mn in Apr-2026 and the rest of the provision is held for others. We value on EPS before exceptional items (as the street does) but treat litigation as a recurring cost of the US business in our risks.

**Forex in the headline.** The company's headline EBITDA includes forex and other income: FY26 33.6% vs 29.7% without them; the FY26 forex gain was ₹657 cr (2.4% of sales) from a weaker rupee. Our EBITDA (and Screener's annual figure) excludes both; we forecast no forex gains.

**Costs below EBITDA.** The $75mn Mirabegron prepaid option was capitalised and is amortised to Sep-2027 (~₹434 cr in FY27E), so part of the cost of keeping Mirabegron on the market never touches EBITDA. EV/EBITDA comparisons flatter Lupin for that reason.

**Other income.** FY26 other income ₹424 cr: ₹371 cr of treasury income on ~₹8,000 cr average gross cash, ₹35 cr of one-offs (a business-divestment gain, asset-sale gains) and ₹19 cr miscellaneous. We build it from these parts (see Forecasts).
**Tax.** ETR 22.1% in FY26 (incentives and deferred tax), 29.8% in Q1FY27, guided 27-28% for FY27: ~7% of EPS lost to tax alone.
**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow ₹7,334 cr in FY26 (90% of EBITDA), helped by working capital falling from 110 to 87 days; free cash flow after capex (incl. the Mirabegron licence) ₹5,279 cr.

**Contingent items.** ₹635 cr of guarantees for subsidiaries, ₹150 cr of disputed tax demands, ₹68 cr of other claims (AR FY26 note 40), plus the open-ended US antitrust litigation (no estimate possible, per the company).

**Minorities and audit.** Minorities are small (₹22.6 cr in FY26, mainly the Philippines); we use profit attributable to owners. Auditor B S R & Co. (KPMG network), unqualified; goodwill impairment testing is a key audit matter.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The accounts are audited cleanly and segment data is published every quarter, but reported profit has been hit by large litigation and impairment charges in four of the last seven years, the headline margin includes forex, and Screener misclassifies forex and exceptional items. Lupin does not disclose sales of its key US products, so investors cannot see the windfall directly.

sections.title: Balance sheet: ₹10,600 cr of gross cash, ₹6,600 cr of debt; net cash ~₹4,000 cr

blocks.p: Lupin carries both cash and debt. At Mar-2026 it held ₹10,594 cr of cash, liquid funds and bank deposits (including ₹1,364 cr deposited against a US term loan) and owed ₹6,616 cr: US-dollar term loans at SOFR + 1.0-1.2%, short-term working-capital loans and ₹706 cr of leases. The company reports net cash of ₹4,636 cr (it leaves out leases); our model starts from ₹3,978 cr, the same gross cash less all borrowings including leases. Goodwill and other intangibles rose from ₹4,571 cr to ₹5,545 cr in FY26 (the Mirabegron licence, product rights) and will rise again with VISUfarma. Working capital improved: the company's operating working capital fell from 110 days of sales (Mar-25) to 87 days (Mar-26), then rose to 90 days in June as sales jumped.

Large one-off gains or charges shown separately (FY26: antitrust provision, Mirabegron settlement, labour codes, settlement and arbitration income).
The first generic applicant challenging a patent, eligible for 180 days of exclusivity ("exclusive" if no one else shares it).
Form 483 / VAI / OAI / EIR / warning letter

USFDA inspection observations / Voluntary Action Indicated (minor) / Official Action Indicated (serious) / Establishment Inspection Report closing an inspection / formal letter that blocks new approvals from a site.
Share price divided by the next full fiscal year's EPS.
Indian pharmaceutical market / the data provider that tracks pharmacy-level sales and US prescriptions.
Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy: a USFDA safety programme that restricts how a drug is dispensed (Tolvaptan).
Return on equity (profit ÷ shareholders' funds) / return on capital employed.
The median of the nine-peer pharma set's P/E at 30-Sep-2026 vs their five-year medians (+8.2%), applied to Lupin's own historical multiple.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Lupin (consolidated, Rs crore; profit attributable to owners, see tools/authoring/LUPIN.patch.js). Lupin reports one operating segment and sales by market, so the engine runs on one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the market build (US in US dollars x an assumed rupee rate) sits in `businessLines` and LUPIN.ctx.js checks that it sums to model revenue. Screener 'Sales' = revenue from operations incl. other operating income (export/PLI incentives); EBITDA excludes forex and other income (company definition; Screener's annual operating profit is on the same basis). Other income = treasury yield x opening net cash + the same yield on gross debt (gross cash = net cash + gross debt) + recurring misc income, less the yield on the VISUfarma payment in FY27. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by market (businessLines; the script checks the sum). FY27E +7.7%: guidance is high-single-digit growth in product sales (rupee terms). US USD1,170mn (guided USD1.1-1.2bn: Q1 USD366mn, then USD250-280mn a quarter as Apotex and Teva enter Tolvaptan and Mirabegron pressure runs a full quarter; upper half of the range given Q1 and Lupin's record of beating guidance) at Rs95.0/US$ (Q1 implied Rs93.9; Rs95.8 on 30-Sep). India +13% (Q1 +13.9%, Rx +15.1% vs IPM +13.5%; guided 1.2-1.3x IPM; FY26 base depressed by tender sales and in-licensed product LOEs). Other developed markets +39% (VISUfarma consolidated from Apr-2026, EUR53mn revenue in 2025; Q1 +48%). Emerging markets +16% (Q1 +52% but a higher base from Q2FY26). API +6%. Other operating income Rs260 cr (PLI lower: Rs60 cr in Q1). FY28E +9.1%: US USD1,200mn (+3%: apixaban oral suspension launch around summer 2027 with 10-12 months before generics, full year of pegfilgrastim, ivacaftor exclusivity, nasal sprays, offset by further Tolvaptan erosion and broad Mirabegron entry from Sep-2027) at Rs97; India +12%, Europe-led ODM +13% (guided 10-20%), EM +11%. FY29E +6.4%: US USD1,150mn (apixaban generics enter, Mirabegron and Tolvaptan tails; Dulera, Respimat and biosimilars only start) at Rs99; India +12%, ODM +12%, EM +10%.

businessLines._why: Product sales by market, FY26 (Q4FY26 press release): US Rs11,678.3 cr (USD1,318mn: Rs88.6/US$), India Rs8,114.0 cr, other developed markets Rs3,243.9 cr, emerging markets Rs3,482.8 cr, API Rs968.5 cr; other operating income Rs470.5 cr. Total Rs27,958.0 cr = Screener revenue. US in dollars x rupee rate (2% a year weaker from Rs95.0 in FY27E).

assumptions._marginWhy: EBITDA excl. forex and other income on revenue from operations (Screener basis): 23.2% FY25, 29.2% FY26 (company basis on product sales: 23.8% and 29.7%); Q1FY27 30.0% (company). Guidance: ~25% for FY27 (CFO: 'in the range of 24% to 25%' with gross margin moderating as Tolvaptan prices fall and raw material costs rise). FY27E 25.3% (= 25.5% on product sales): Q2-Q4 at ~23.8% after Q1's 30%. FY28E 23.8%: a full year without Tolvaptan pricing and with Mirabegron opened up from Sep-2027, partly offset by apixaban (limited competition), India and Europe operating leverage and adjacencies (100-150bp drag) moving to breakeven; R&D ~8% of sales. FY29E 23.0%: apixaban fades; street FY28E 22.9-26.1% (Emkay 22.9%, PL 23.4%, MOSL 23.6%, BOB 26.1%); Citi sees ~20% by FY29. Each 1pp of margin is ~Rs330 cr of EBITDA (~5% of FY28E EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27E includes the VISUfarma acquisition (enterprise value EUR190mn, ~Rs1,970 cr, cash-funded, closed 2-Apr-2026) so that net cash at Mar-27 is right; organic capex Rs1,700 cr (Q1 Rs279 cr; FY26 Rs1,062 cr). ICRA (8-Jul-2026): capex Rs3,500-4,000 cr in FY27 including VISUfarma and Rs1,000-1,500 cr in FY28. FY28E Rs1,300 cr, FY29E Rs1,400 cr (~4% of sales). In-licensing and further acquisitions are not modelled.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation, amortisation and impairment Rs1,375.5 cr; Q1FY27 Rs452.9 cr (Rs1,812 cr annualised), of which ~Rs107 cr is amortisation of the USD75mn Mirabegron prepaid option (Feb-2026 to Sep-2027, ~USD3.8mn a month). Bottom-up: base D&A Rs346 cr a quarter (incl. VISUfarma intangibles) plus ~7% on new capex = Rs1,443 / 1,548 / 1,643 cr for FY27-29E, plus the licence Rs434 / 222 / 0 cr = Rs1,877 / 1,770 / 1,643 cr (Rs5,290 cr in three years). The engine uses one rate on gross block (Screener Rs23,217 cr at Mar-26, plus capex incl. VISUfarma); 6.5% matches the three-year total (FY27E Rs1,628 cr, ~Rs250 cr below the bottom-up; FY28-29E Rs20-235 cr above it), so Sep-28E EPS carries a ~2% conservative bias. At 7.2% (FY27E = the Q1 run-rate; D&A rising like Emkay's Rs1,953 / 2,124 cr for FY28-29E) Sep-28E EPS would be ~3% lower: see the valuation sensitivity.

otherTreasury._why: Screener counts cash and bank balances Rs5,653 cr and investments Rs3,670 cr (of which Rs92.5 cr are non-current strategic and equity-method investments) against borrowings incl. leases of Rs6,616 cr, and misses Rs1,364 cr of earmarked bank deposits held in other non-current financial assets (AR FY26 note 10; they back a US term loan). Adjustment +1,364.0 - 92.5 = +Rs1,271.5 cr, so the model's opening net cash is Rs3,978 cr: company-basis gross cash Rs10,594 cr less all borrowings incl. Rs706 cr of leases. The company's own net cash (Rs4,636 cr) excludes leases (and differs by a further ~Rs48 cr we cannot reconcile). The VISUfarma payment is in FY27E capex.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: FY26 treasury income Rs371.2 cr (deposit interest Rs156.7 cr + CP/debenture interest Rs60.2 cr + mutual-fund gains Rs97.0 cr realised and Rs57.3 cr unrealised, AR FY26 note 31) on average gross cash of ~Rs8,000 cr (Rs5,412 cr at Mar-25, Rs10,594 cr at Mar-26) = 4.6%; Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 run at ~5.6-5.9% annualised as cash built up. 5.5% on gross cash. The engine applies the yield to opening net cash; the gross-debt part sits in otherIncome below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-net-cash parts of other income: (a) 5.5% x opening gross debt incl. leases (Rs6,616 / 6,336 / 6,056 cr: ICRA expects repayments of Rs270-290 cr a year; we use Rs280 cr), because the company earns on gross cash = net cash + gross debt; (b) recurring miscellaneous income Rs20 cr (FY26 Rs18.8 cr); less (c) in FY27E, 5.5% on the Rs1,970 cr VISUfarma payment made on 2-Apr-2026, which the engine's opening net cash still includes. FY27E total other income Rs494 cr vs Rs424.5 cr in FY26 (Rs390 cr recurring after Rs34.5 cr of one-offs: business-divestment gain, asset-sale gains, fair-value gain on a non-current investment) and Rs475.7 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26. Forex gains (Rs656.5 cr in FY26; a Rs13.9 cr loss in Q1FY27) are not forecast.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs434.5 cr on average borrowings incl. leases of ~Rs6,030 cr (7.2%); Q1FY27 Rs109.6 cr (Rs438 cr annualised). 6.8% on average gross debt falling Rs280 cr a year (USD term loans at SOFR + 1.0-1.2%, packing credit, leases, other charges).
assumptions._taxWhy: ETR 22.1% in FY26 and 29.8% in Q1FY27; guided 27-28% for FY27 (Q1 call; 25-26% in May) as incentives on some Indian plants phase out. 27.5% / 27% / 27% (Emkay 27%).
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs18 a share (900% on Rs2; ~Rs823 cr) = 15.4% of EPS; management keeps cash for specialty acquisitions and R&D.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash and a large Indian branded business, but ~40% of sales and most of the profit swings in the US with exclusivities, approvals, inspections and antitrust litigation; two loss years since FY20. Ke 11.9% (Cipla 11.3% at beta 0.8).
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%: India ~10-12% nominal, US generics flat to low single digit in dollars, Europe and EM high single digit; a rupee blend near 5.5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth moves from ~6% to 7% as India, Europe and EM outgrow a flattish US.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 22%: between FY25 (23.2%) and Citi's ~20%; no new windfall assumed, but complex launches keep the US above its FY23 trough.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 4.5% of revenue (FY26 3.9% organic; FY27 ~5.6% organic incl. growth projects); depreciation 4.5% of revenue (FY26 4.9% incl. impairment and the Mirabegron licence).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Management's view plays out: apixaban oral suspension becomes a Tolvaptan-sized product, ivacaftor and nasal-spray exclusivities land, biosimilars reach a couple of hundred million dollars across the US and Europe, and the US is back above USD300mn a quarter in FY28 (BOB).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Citi's case: the US base keeps losing share and price, falling towards USD975mn by FY29; apixaban is short-lived; a Spiriva generic arrives; margin heads to ~20%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Lupin: every note that discloses a method uses P/E (Motilal Oswal 22x 12-month-forward, Prabhudas Lilladher 25x FY28E, BOB Capital Markets 26x Jun-28E). 19x = Lupin's 17.6x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items (FY26 net exceptional charge Rs557.9 cr; batch practice A18), leaving out the trough year FY23 (forward EPS Rs9.45, below half of FY21's Rs26.81: dates Apr-2021 to Mar-2022, when the P/E ran at 80-125x), times the pharma sector factor of 1.082 (median of the nine-peer set's trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +8.2%, PLAYBOOK §7c; Lupin is outside the set) = 19.1x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. The windfalls (gSpiriva, Mirabegron, Tolvaptan) stay in the base (§7c). No growth or returns adjustment. Bull 22.5x and bear 17x: the 75th (20.8x) and 25th (15.9x) percentiles of the same series times the same factor.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (EV = price x shares + Screener net debt at the latest March; EBITDA = next full year, ours for FY27-28E): median 11.9x (no trough years by the half-of-peak rule), times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor for the same nine peers (+7.46%) = 12.8x, rounded to 13x; bull/bear from the 75th/25th percentiles (14.1x / 9.4x).
